title: A question with no searchable word crashes Ask AI on MySQL (ORDER BY 0)
evidence: questionPriority(): `$terms = array_slice(array_values(array_filter($this->extractRawTokens($question), fn (string $t) => strlen($t) >= 3)), 0, 8); if ($terms === []) { return ['0', []]; }` and buildKnowledgeCorpus() line 3345 `->orderByRaw($orgOrder, $orgOrderBindings)` (again at 3414). Live, POST /api/ai/assistant/ask {"question":"What can you do?"} returned 500 for all five roles: `SQLSTATE[42S22]: Unknown column '0' in 'order clause' ... from organizations where id in (2) order by 0, name asc limit 30`. POST /api/ai/assistant/chat {"message":"What is it?"} ended with `event: error {"message":"Could not answer that right now. Try again."}`. SQLite rejects it too (`1st ORDER BY term out of range`), so no test asks such a question.
impact: Any question whose words are all stopwords or shorter than three letters ("What can you do?", "What is it?", "Who am I?", "ok", "so?") throws a QueryException. ask() and deterministicAnswer() always build the record list, so this hits every role and every data intent (only refusals and how-to guides return before it), on the dashboard Ask AI box (one-shot /ask, a 500) and in the chat page (error bubble). "What can you do?" is the most likely first question a new user types into the dashboard box.
fix: Make questionPriority() return null when there are no terms and guard both call sites: `->when($orgOrder !== null, fn ($q) => $q->orderByRaw($orgOrder, $orgOrderBindings))` (same for $leaderOrder). Do not replace '0' with '(0)' (SQLite still rejects it). Add a test in AskAiRetrievalAuditFixesTest that posts "What can you do?" and "What is it?" to /api/ai/assistant/ask for each role and expects 200.

title: Ordinary money questions are still routed to staff intents: a student asking for an outstanding balance or a fee deadline is refused
evidence: INTENT_PATTERNS is ordered and `'missing_requirements' => '~\b(?:missing|incomplete|lacking|outstanding|requirements?|compliance|deadlines?|accreditation)\b~'` and `'pending_approvals' => '~\b(?:approvals?|approve|...)~'` sit above `'finance_health'`. Live as student 2100142: "What is my outstanding balance?" -> intent missing_submissions, title "Not available for your access", answer "A student account does not have access to the compliance files that organizations send to the SAO...". Same refusal for "When is the deadline to pay my fees?" and "I am missing a receipt for my payment"; "Is my payment still pending approval?" -> pending_approvals refusal; "What new events were assigned this month?" -> tasks_workload refusal. As Admin 900001, "What is our outstanding balance?" and "Which students have an outstanding balance?" return the compliance answer ("...has 1 unsubmitted or returned compliance requirement...").
impact: This is askai-core-02 again in the new table: the most common student question about money (what do I owe, by when) gets a refusal about compliance files, and an Admin asking about balances gets the compliance list. A student who is refused once stops asking.
fix: In classifyIntent, decide by role before the generic words: for STUDENT, try the student intents first (finance_health words `balance|owe|fees?|invoices?|pay(?:ment|ments)?|receipts?|dues`, then clearances, orders, elections, events) and only fall to a staff intent when none matches; for every role, move the money words that are unambiguous (`balances?|owe[ds]?|unpaid|invoices?|fees?|receipts?`) above `missing_requirements`, and drop the bare `outstanding`, `deadlines?` and `missing` from `missing_requirements` unless a compliance word (`requirements?|compliance|files?|documents?|reports?|accreditation|submit\w*`) is also present. Add these exact questions to the routing table test in AskAiCoreAuditFixesTest for STUDENT and ADMIN.

title: Department Head asking what is waiting for 'my endorsement' is told nothing is waiting while budget and event requests are
evidence: asksApplications(): `if (preg_match('/\bendors(e|es|ed|ing|ement|ements)\b/', $q) === 1) { return true; }` and AskAiService::classifyIntent line 309 consults `$this->roleIntents->match($question, $role)` before every INTENT_PATTERNS entry. The Department Head briefing itself calls approval requests endorsements (AskAiService line 1005: `'budget or event request')).' '.$this->be($pendingApprovals).' waiting for your endorsement.'`). Live as 940001: briefing says "today you have 2 requests waiting for your endorsement"; "What is waiting for my endorsement?" and "Which budget requests are waiting for my endorsement?" -> intent applications_queue, answer "No applications are waiting for your endorsement right now.", highlights 0 / 0. The two pending requests (Sports Fest 2024 Budget, Induction and Recognition Ceremony) are not mentioned.
impact: A dean who uses the product's own word gets a false all-clear for the role's main job. The same takeover happens for the SAO with any question containing 'endorse'.
fix: In asksApplications() require the word application/registration as well: return true only when `\b(applications?|applicants?)\b` is present together with an endorse/approve/waiting word. In buildApplicationsQueue, when the queue is empty, read the count of the role's pending approval requests (same scope as AskAiService::buildPendingApprovals) and say it in the answer ("No applications are waiting, but 2 budget or event requests are waiting for your endorsement") so the two queues never contradict each other. Add both questions to AskAiRoleIntentsTest::match near misses and to the routing test (expected pending_approvals).

title: 'Venue' and 'booking' questions go to the approvals answer, which never reads venue bookings: the SAO is told nothing is waiting with 2 bookings pending
evidence: INTENT_PATTERNS: `'pending_approvals' => '~\b(?:approvals?|approve|approving|endorse\w*|pending review|...|venues?|bookings?|(?:pending|new|waiting|awaiting) registrations?|applications?)\b~'`. buildPendingApprovals (1822-1941) reads only ApprovalRequest and, for the SAO, organizations with lifecycle_status pending; venue_bookings is never queried there, although the SAO briefing counts it (line 808 `$pendingVenues = DB::table('venue_bookings')->where('status', 'pending')->count();`). Live as SAO 990001 (venue_bookings has 2 rows with status pending): "What venue bookings are waiting for me?" -> pending_approvals, "0 approval requests are waiting for your review, and 0 student organizations are waiting for a registration decision." The briefing for the same account says "2 venue bookings". The new test only pins the route: AskAiCoreAuditFixesTest line 148 `['Which venue bookings are pending?', 'SUPER_ADMIN', 'pending_approvals']`.
impact: The SAO asks about bookings and reads an all-clear while two organizations wait for a venue. The briefing's own follow-up chip ("What registrations, event files, and venue bookings are pending?") lands on the same answer. The routing test passes while the answer is wrong.
fix: In buildPendingApprovals for SUPER_ADMIN add a 'Venue bookings waiting for SAO' section and highlight from VenueBooking::where('status','pending') (count separately, oldest first, ROW_LIMIT, href linkTo($user, '/dashboard/super-admin/venues')), and name the count in the answer. For ADMIN, send venue/booking questions to my_submissions (which already reads the organization's bookings) instead of pending_approvals. Extend the routing test to assert the answer names the pending booking, not only the intent.

title: Role-intent matcher runs before every existing pattern and its loose patterns take questions the existing builders answered
evidence: AskAiService line 309-312 returns `$this->roleIntents->match(...)` before the INTENT_PATTERNS loop. Patterns: asksSubmissions `preg_match('/\b(my|our) (\w+ )?(submissions|proposals)\b/', $q)` and `"/\bwhere (is|are|did) (my|our) (\w+ ){0,3}{$thing}\b/"` with $thing including `events?|budgets?|reports?`; toolFor `'announcement_draft' => '/\b(write|draft|compose|writing|drafting)\b.*\bannouncements?\b...'`, `'event_planning' => '...|\bhelp (me|us) plan\b|...'`, `'report_summary' => '/\b(summari[sz]e|...|summary of)\b.*\b(financial )?reports?\b...'`. Live: Admin "What are our missing submissions?" -> my_submissions ("Nothing has been returned to you. 2 submissions are with reviewers...") instead of missing_submissions; Admin "What is the status of my clearance requests?" -> my_submissions; Admin "Where is our event being held tomorrow?" -> my_submissions; Admin "Which draft announcements are still unpublished?" -> ai_tools (tool explainer); Department Head "Summarize the reports waiting for my approval" -> ai_tools instead of pending_approvals; officer "Help me plan my week" -> "Event planning is only for your organization's Admin, so you cannot open it."
impact: Everyday Admin, officer and Department Head questions that already had a correct data answer now get the submissions tracker or a tool description, and an officer is told they lack access to a tool they did not ask for.
fix: Tighten the matchers: drop the bare `(my|our) (submissions|proposals)` alternative (or exclude questions containing missing|late|overdue|compliance|haven't); in the `where is/are` form exclude a following `held|happening|located|taking place|at\b` and require the noun to end the clause; require `draft` to be a verb (`^|\b(?:help me |can you |please )?(?:write|draft|compose)\b ... announcement`), not match `draft announcements`; require `plan` to be followed by event/activity (remove `help (me|us) plan`); for report_summary require `financial report` or `our|the report` without `waiting|approval|pending`. Add each live question above as a near miss in AskAiRoleIntentsTest and as a row of the classifyIntent table test.

title: The 'no invented names' check throws away honest model answers and lets an invented name at the start of a sentence through; it has no test
evidence: namesOnlyKnownPeople(): `foreach (preg_split('/(?<=[.!?:])\s+|\n+/u', $text) ?: [] as $sentence) { if (preg_match_all('/(?<=[\p{Ll},;(]\s)\p{Lu}[\p{L}\'-]+(?:\s+\p{Lu}[\p{L}\'-]+)+/u', $sentence, $matches) < 1) { continue; } ... if (! isset($known[Str::lower($word)])) { return false; }`. Run through tinker against the real method with the facts of a budget and an approvals answer: REJECT "The Student Affairs Office approved both of them."; REJECT "Open Budget Allocation to see each one." (the page the row links to); REJECT "Check the Financial Reports page for details."; REJECT "you can open the Task Board to follow up."; REJECT "both from the College of Computer Studies." (the asker's own scope, which is not in $facts); REJECT "Next, the Department Head reviews the Sports Fest request." KEEP "Maria Santos should review the Sports Fest 2024 Budget first."; KEEP "Two requests are waiting. Rodrigo Duterte sent both of them."; KEEP "Good news, Marco: both budgets are approved." No test in server/tests names this method or sends a model answer with an unknown name.
impact: On the one-shot path (dashboard Ask AI box, enhanceWithModel) a paid model call of up to the provider timeout is made and then discarded whenever the model writes an office, page or college name with capitals, so users wait longer for the same fixed text; yet the thing it exists to stop, a made-up person, passes whenever the name opens a sentence or is one word. The cost is not buying the protection.
fix: Either remove the check and rely on the instruction plus the numeric guard, or make it do its job: (1) match capitalised multi-word phrases anywhere, including sentence start, but skip the first word of a sentence when it is a common word; (2) build the allowed vocabulary from the facts plus a fixed product list (Student Affairs Office, SAO, Department Head, Dean, Organization Admin, Adviser, SBO Officer, page titles from the sidebar such as Budget Allocation, Financial Reports, Task Board, Statement of Account, month and weekday names) and the asker's scopeLabel() and first name, which enhanceWithModel should add to $facts; (3) add tests in AskAiRetrievalAuditFixesTest: an answer naming an unknown person at sentence start and mid-sentence is dropped, and answers containing 'Student Affairs Office', 'Department Head', a page title and the user's college are kept.

title: The daily briefing was not given the builders' fixes, so it disagrees with the answers its own chips open
evidence: Orders: briefing line 1243-1249 `->where('status', 'pending')->where('officer_review_status', 'pending')->whereNotNull('payment_proof_url')` versus buildMerchandiseOrders line 2294-2296 `...->where(fn ($ready) => $ready->whereNotNull('orders.payment_proof_url')->orWhereNull('orders.payment_method')->orWhere('orders.payment_method', '!=', 'gcash'))` (also what DashboardBriefingService::ordersToVerifyAttention uses). Live as Admin 900001 and officer 900004: briefing highlight "Orders to verify=0" and no order row, while "Which merchandise orders need my attention?" says "1 order is waiting for payment verification" (ORD-1, cash). Grievances: briefing line 809-812 `DB::table('grievances')->whereNotIn('status', ['resolved', 'dismissed'])->whereRaw('LOWER(urgency) in (?, ?)', ['high', 'critical'])->count()` has no `whereNull('deleted_at')`; buildGrievancesStatus line 2681-2683 has it. Semester: briefing line 1230-1231 and 1256-1260 count tasks and ended events with no semester filter; buildTasksWorkload line 2050-2052 and buildEventsAttendance line 2392/2411 filter by AcademicSemester::selected(). Approvals: briefing lines 799-800, 978-982 and 1240 count every pending request for the role; buildPendingApprovals line 1839-1848 also requires `assigned_approver` null or the user and the SAO entity types.
impact: An Admin or officer with a cash order waiting is told there is nothing to verify; the SAO is told to read urgent grievances that the student has withdrawn (soft-deleted) and then finds none; after a semester change the briefing shows last semester's overdue tasks and the Tasks page it links to shows none; a request assigned to another approver is counted as waiting for you.
fix: In buildDailyPriorities reuse the builders' own definitions: extract the three order filters, the open-grievance query (with whereNull('deleted_at')), the awaiting-approvals query (required_role, assigned_approver, SAO entity types, organization scope) and the semester filter for tasks and events into private methods and call them from both the briefing and the builders. Add a test per pair that seeds one cash order, one soft-deleted urgent grievance, one overdue task in another semester and one request assigned to another approver, and asserts the briefing and the builder report the same count.

title: 'Where is my submission' tells the Admin a reviewer decides next when the request is waiting for the Admin's own approval
evidence: `private const APPROVAL_TYPES = ['event', 'budget', 'election', 'announcement', 'financial_report'];` (line 37), `private const REVIEWER_NAMES = ['DEPARTMENT_HEAD' => 'the Department Head', 'SUPER_ADMIN' => 'SAO'];` (57-60), row status `'Waiting for '.($reviewer ?? 'a reviewer')` (495), answer `'Nothing has been returned to you. %s with reviewers%s. The oldest, %s, was sent %s, and the reviewer decides next.'` (369), and for rejected rows `'%s come back to you for changes. Start with %s, returned by %s%s. Fix it and send it again; the next move is yours.'` (361). server/config/approvals.php: `'announcement' => 'ADMIN'`, so an officer's announcement creates an ApprovalRequest with required_role ADMIN for the same organization (AnnouncementController line 446).
impact: An Admin with an officer's announcement in their own queue asks "Where is our announcement?" and reads "1 announcement is with reviewers ... the reviewer decides next" with status "Waiting for a reviewer": the one person who must act is told to wait. An announcement the Admin rejected is reported back to the Admin as "returned to you ... fix it and send it again".
fix: In latestApprovals/submissionItems treat required_role ADMIN separately: count pending ADMIN-stage requests as 'Waiting for you' (status 'Waiting for you', tone warning, href /dashboard/approvals, listed first, answer "1 announcement from your officers is waiting for your approval"), and show ADMIN-stage rejections as 'You returned this to <requester>' instead of 'Returned to you'. Add REVIEWER_NAMES['ADMIN'] => 'you'. Test with an announcement approval pinned to required_role ADMIN, status pending and rejected.

title: Student 'Can I vote' answer never checks the voter list or the ballot, though the chip promises 'whether you have already voted'
evidence: buildElectionsStatus counts `->whereIn('elections.status', ['active', 'upcoming'])->whereNull('elections.cancelled_at')->when($memberView, fn ($elections) => $elections->whereNotNull('elections.finalized_at'))` and answers `'%d %s open for voting now, and %d %s coming up.'`; it never calls Election::listsVoter() or ElectionBallot::hasVoted(), which unvotedElections() (line 766-785) uses for the briefing, and it ignores the runoff phase that unvotedElections() includes (`->orWhere('phase', 'runoff')`). Starter prompt line 4417: `'description' => 'The elections open to you, and whether you have already voted.'`. Live as student: "Did I already vote?" -> "1 election is open for voting now, and 0 elections are coming up." with an "Open election" link to /dashboard/elections/cast-vote.
impact: A student who has voted, or who is not on the voter list, is told an election is open and sent to the ballot page; a student in a runoff is told nothing is open. The question the chip asks is not answered for anyone.
fix: For memberView, build the rows from the same source as the briefing: for each election the student's votingOrganizationIds() cover, use openRound(), listsVoter($user->school_id) and ElectionBallot::hasVoted() to set the row status to 'You can vote now', 'You have voted' or 'You are not on the voter list', and write the answer from those counts ("You can vote in 1 election now; you have already voted in 0."). Link 'Cast vote' only when the student can vote. Test with a voted student, an unlisted student and a runoff.

title: Clearance answers show role constants and never say who has not signed
evidence: Student rows: `'primary' => Str::upper($sig->required_role).' — '.($sig->org_name ?: 'University'),` (2505); staff rows: `'secondary' => $r->remarks ?: 'Stage: '.Str::upper($r->required_role),` (2583) and `'meta' => Str::upper($r->required_role),` (2586). Student answer (2483): `'On your clearance, %d %s signed, %d %s pending and %d %s on hold.'`. Live as student 2100142, "Who hasn't signed my clearance yet, and why?" -> "On your clearance, 2 signatures are signed, 1 is pending and 0 are on hold." with rows "ORGANIZATION — Philippine Society of Information Technology Students - College of Computer Studies", "DEPARTMENT_HEAD — Philippine Society of ...", "SAO — Philippine Society of ..." (status "Pending"). As Department Head: secondary "Stage: DEPARTMENT_HEAD", meta "DEPARTMENT_HEAD"; as officer: "Stage: ORGANIZATION".
impact: The student's starter prompt asks who has not signed and why; the sentence gives counts only, and the list labels the dean and the SAO with system constants and the student organization's name. This is the dean's 'say who owns the next move' point on the screen students open most.
fix: Map required_role to words once (organization => the organization's name, department_head => 'Department Head', sao => 'SAO') and use it in both branches: student primary "Department Head" / "SAO" / organization name, status 'Waiting for SAO' or 'Held by the Department Head', and an answer that names them ("Your organization and the Department Head have signed. The SAO has not signed yet." plus the hold remark when held). In the staff rows replace 'Stage: X' and the meta with 'Waiting for your signature' / 'On hold'. Assert no upper-case role constant appears in the payload for each role.

title: Grievance questions from anyone but the SAO return unrelated search results at 99% match; the audited Admin gap (askai-rag-19) is still open
evidence: classifyIntent: `'grievances_status' => $role === 'SUPER_ADMIN' ? 'grievances_status' : 'semantic_rag',` and buildGrievancesStatus line 2677 `if ($user->role !== 'SUPER_ADMIN') { return $this->buildDailyPriorities(...); }`. Grievances are not in buildKnowledgeCorpus. GrievanceController::index gives the Admin `->where('organization_id', $request->user()->organization_id)` and the student their own. Live: Admin "Are there urgent student grievances?" -> "Found 13 matching record(s) out of 59 checked across 4 area(s) (best match: 99%). Key findings: HIUSA Student Council Election 2024-2025 Now Open (Published — Published); ... Juan Dela Vega — Candidate for President (Active — UP)."; student "What happened to my grievance?" -> announcements, a candidate and a venue. STUDENT_REDIRECTS['grievances_status'] (line 95) can never be reached by a typed question.
impact: An organization head with grievances addressed to the organization (2 open in the seeded data, one High) is shown election candidates and venues as a confident match, and a student asking about their own grievance gets announcements. Nobody is pointed to the Grievances or My grievances page.
fix: Return 'grievances_status' for every role in classifyIntent. In buildGrievancesStatus: ADMIN reads Grievance::where('organization_id', $user->organization_id) (no names, same columns as the SAO branch) with href linkTo($user, '/dashboard/grievances'); STUDENT reads only their own (submitted_by = school_id) with status and href /dashboard/my-grievances and is added to STUDENT_INTENTS; SBO_OFFICER and DEPARTMENT_HEAD get one sentence saying grievances are read by the organization head and the SAO. Add tests for each role, including that an Admin never sees another organization's or SAO-addressed grievances.

title: System and engine wording is still in what people read
evidence: Record-search answer (3188): `'Found %d matching record(s) out of %d checked across %d area(s) (best match: %d%%). Key findings: %s.'` with items built by (3180) `sprintf('%s (%s — %s)', $c['primary'], $c['status'], $c['meta'] ?: $c['secondary'])`; live: "Found 11 matching record(s) out of 56 checked across 4 area(s) (best match: 99%). Key findings: HIUSA Student Council Election 2024-2025 Now Open (Published — Published)". Related section (3269): `'Additional cross-domain records matching '.implode(...)`, empty text `'No additional cross-domain matches.'`. Finance answer (2221): `'Approved budgets in scope total ₱%s allocated with ₱%s remaining...'`; also `'No approved budgets recorded in scope.'` (2238), `'Every organization in scope has submitted...'` (1532), `'Every active organization in scope has an assigned administrator.'` (1994). Row text (1998): `'Active organization with no active ADMIN profile'`. Approval row status (1867): `'Pending '.$this->roleName($req->required_role)` -> "Pending Department Head" live, "Pending Super Admin" for the SAO. roleName() (4178) gives "Super Admin", used in the capabilities answer (210): live "As Super Admin for University-wide student organizations, you can ask me things like". Organization rows (3361): `'College: %s · Lifecycle: %s · Accreditation: %s'`. Chart subtitle (2919): `'Distribution across %d matching record(s)'`; stock (3617) `'... Stock: %d unit(s)'`. API labels: (481) `'engine' => 'Procedural Knowledge RAG (BM25 + Trigram over role guides)'`, roleLabel() (4168-4172) `'SAO Operations Copilot'` ... `'Student Portal Copilot'` returned as role_label by GET /api/ai/assistant.
impact: The dean asked for plain human wording. The record-search answer is the fallback for every question the patterns do not catch, so "record(s)", "area(s)", "best match: 99%" and "Published — Published" are what many first answers look like; the SAO is called "Super Admin"; a waiting row says "Pending Super Admin" instead of "Waiting for SAO". The engine and Copilot labels are not rendered by the current client but are in the API responses the audit said to clean.
fix: Use $this->plural() for records/areas/units; drop the percentage from sentences a person reads (keep it in rag_metadata) and write the key findings as `primary (status)` without repeating the status as meta; rename the section description to 'Other records that mention <term>.'; replace 'in scope' with 'your organization's' / 'your college's' / 'all organizations'' by role; 'Active organization with no active ADMIN profile' -> 'No organization head has been named yet'; status -> 'Waiting for '.('SUPER_ADMIN' => 'SAO', 'DEPARTMENT_HEAD' => 'the Department Head', 'ADMIN' => 'the organization head'); roleName('SUPER_ADMIN') -> 'the SAO' (and 'an organization head', 'a student' in the capabilities sentence); 'Lifecycle:' -> 'Status:'; rag_metadata.engine for guides -> 'HIUSA guides'; roleLabel values -> 'SAO assistant', 'College assistant', 'Organization assistant', 'Officer assistant', 'Student assistant'. Add an assertion over every intent's payload that it contains none of '(s)', 'in scope', 'cross-domain', 'Copilot', 'RAG', 'BM25', 'SUPER_ADMIN', 'DEPARTMENT_HEAD', 'SBO_OFFICER', 'Super Admin'.

title: Student answers are worded for staff and offer chips that are then refused
evidence: buildEventsAttendance uses one text for all roles (2419): `'%d %s upcoming or ongoing, and %d past %s still open and should be marked completed.'`, highlight `'Needs closing'` (2427) and follow-up (2448) `['topic' => 'missing_submissions', 'label' => 'Missing event files?', ...]`. buildSemanticRagPayload follow-ups (3225-3234) are fixed for every role: `'missing_submissions' ... "Who hasn't submitted compliance or financial reports?"` and `'finance_health' ... 'How is our budget utilization and financial status?'`. A student account does not have access to the compliance files...". The student record-search answer carries "Check missing submissions" and "Review financial health".

Pass every builder's follow_ups through one filter in answer(): drop any follow-up whose topic fails intentAllowed($user, $topic), and in buildSemanticRagPayload take the follow-ups from starterPrompts($user) instead of the fixed list. Test: no follow-up in any student payload has a topic outside STUDENT_INTENTS or fee_usage.

title: Officer briefing tells the officer to upload compliance files, which only the Admin can do
evidence: buildDailyPriorities for ADMIN and SBO_OFFICER shares one row (1288-1298): `'primary' => 'Upload your missing compliance files', ... 'href' => $this->routeAccess->hrefFor($role, '/dashboard/compliance'), 'action_label' => 'Open compliance'` and the sentence (1342) `'missing or returned compliance requirement'`. /dashboard/compliance is not in the SBO_OFFICER list of client_routes.php. title: SAO and Department Head answers still read archived, pending and returned organizations outside the missing-submissions answer
evidence: scopedStudentOrganizationIds (2819-2823): `return DB::table('organizations')->where('organization_type', 'STUDENT_ORGANIZATION')->pluck('id');` with no lifecycle filter, and the Department Head branch returns every id of the college. activeOrganizationIds() (752-758) is used only in buildDailyPriorities. The other builders pass the unfiltered ids straight in: buildSubmittedDocuments (1680 `$orgIds = $organizationIds->all();`), buildFinanceHealth (2187-2192 `Budget::query()->whereIn('organization_id', $orgIds)->where('submission_status', 'approved')`), buildEventsAttendance (2382-2389), buildTasksWorkload (2037-2043), buildElectionsStatus (2605-2613), and the briefing's `organization_compliance_submissions` count (796-798) has no organization filter at all.
impact: After the SAO archives an organization, its approved budgets stay in the SAO's and the dean's 'allocated / remaining' totals, its approved events stay in 'upcoming', its open tasks in the workload and its submitted files in 'waiting for review'. The fixer brief asked for active organizations only unless the question is about pending or archived ones (askai-builders-02, askai-core-07); only two call sites got it.

Scope the briefing's compliance-submission count with `->whereIn('organization_id', $activeIds)`. Add a test with one archived organization holding an approved budget, an approved future event and a submitted file, asserting none appears for the SAO or the dean.

title: Dean's office staff still get Department Head-only links from guides and record search
evidence: The builders resolve links with the stored profile role (2786 `$this->routeAccess->hrefFor((string) $user->profileRole(), $path)`), but the guides and the record list use the authorizing role: buildHowToGuide (499, 510) `$role = $user->role; ... $this->routeAccess->hrefFor($role, $this->guides->stepPath($step, $role))`, buildHowToCatalog (678), buildKnowledgeCorpus (3329 `$role = $user->role;`, 3945 `'href' => $this->corpusHref($role, 'compliance')` with CORPUS_PAGES compliance => DEPARTMENT_HEAD => '/dashboard/department-head/compliance'). For office staff User::getRoleAttribute returns DEPARTMENT_HEAD on the request while the client is given the stored role ADMIN (User::attributesToArray), and the ADMIN list in client_routes.php holds only /dashboard/department-head/approvals, /documents, /organizations and /people. HowToGuideLibrary has 3 steps on '/dashboard/department-head/compliance' and 2 on '/dashboard/department-head/announcements'.
impact: An office staff account (the dean's delegate) that asks how to review compliance, or gets compliance rows in a search answer, is given 'Go to page' links the client route guard refuses for its role, which is askai-builders-09 again outside the builders.
fix: Use one link resolver everywhere: replace the `$this->routeAccess->hrefFor($role, ...)` calls in buildHowToGuide, buildHowToCatalog, howToReadinessRows, buildDailyPriorities and corpusHref() with linkTo($user, ...) (pass $user into corpusHref), and for office staff fall back to the nearest allowed page ('/dashboard/department-head/documents' for compliance) as complianceReviewLink() already does. Add an office-staff case to AskAiRetrievalAuditFixesTest asserting every href in a guide and a search answer passes ClientRouteAccess for 'ADMIN'.

title: 'Related records' is appended to exact answers whenever a word of the question equals someone's first name, position or acronym
evidence: retrieveRagContext (3082-3087): `foreach ($doc['entity_terms'] ?? [] as $entityTerm) { ... if ($entityLower !== '' && strlen($entityLower) >= 3 && $this->containsWord($questionLower, $entityLower)) { $entityBoost += 1.6; $matchedEntities[$entityTerm] = $entityTerm; } }`; directory rows register `'entity_terms' => array_filter([$fullName, $leader->first_name, $leader->last_name, $position, ...])` (3456); augmentWithRagMatches (3265) adds the section when `$matchedEntities !== [] && $highConfidenceExtras->isNotEmpty()`. Live as SAO: "Which organization applications are waiting for my approval?" -> the applications answer followed by "Related records — Additional cross-domain records matching Organization." listing six "Organization Adviser (Adviser)" directory rows with school ID and email, because the seeded advisers' first name is "Organization". Admin and officer briefings and the officer budget answer show the same block.
impact: A single boost of 1.6 is 73% on its own, so any person called May, Grace, Angel or Joy, or any position word such as President, pulls directory rows with IDs and emails under unrelated staff answers (not students: contact details are hidden for them). It reads as noise and as a 99% match.
fix: Count a person as a matched entity only on the full name or on first name plus last name both present in the question; never on first_name, last_name or position alone. In augmentWithRagMatches require the extra row to share the answer's domain or to be matched by an organization, event or budget title, cap it at three rows, and skip it for the role intents and the briefing.
